newsitem.title: UK: Nigeria's NNPC keeps crude buyers on tenterhooks.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's NNPC keeps crude buyers on tenterhooks.

text.p: State Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) is keeping most of its crude buyers on tenterhooks by letting their contracts expire and rolling them forward on a month-to-month basis, leaving just 10 companies with live contracts, traders said.
NNPC cancelled 21 contracts in March and 12 more from September, but these companies still expect to receive their normal volumes in the fourth quarter of the year.
"Being on tenterhooks has become the norm," a trader in Nigerian crude said.

Of NNPC's 800,000 barrels per day (bpd) exports, traders said just 250,000 bpd was now sold on live term contracts, 150,000 bpd through spot sales and 400,000 bpd on expired contracts rolled over from month to month.

Granted by NNPC, traders say the contracts are under the direct control of Nigerian ruler General Sani Abacha. They are lucrative because most holders sell the oil on to Western traders on commissions worth 8-10 cents per barrel.
NNPC exports about half of Nigeria's total oil exports, with the other half in the hands of the main joint venture production companies including Shell, Mobil, Agip, Chevron and Elf.
